THE JOURNEY CRASHED THE WHOLE RUN ON ONE MISSING RECORD. jrn06's RN5/M-D3 block read d.deaths[d.deaths.length-1].placement_rule with no guard; on one run the death did not register and the TypeError took down eighteen checks that had already passed. Guarded, and the block now REPORTS death_registered:false with the death state attached instead of throwing. Standalone re-run of the same RN5 sequence registered the death normally (deaths.len 1), so the non-registration is intermittent and only reachable deep in a full session.

crime.bounty IN THE SAVE IS A PROJECTION, not a source: sim.stealth.mirrorToSave() rewrites it from crime.ledger every frame, so hand-editing crime.bounty in a blob is silently overwritten within one step. A probe that perturbs it is measuring nothing. Perturb crime.ledger.bounty instead. Found by my own falsifiability control going half-green.

THE JOURNEY WAS MEASURING A STOPPED WORLD AND REPORTING [OK] ON EVERY ROW. Pinned, not guessed: (1) Engine._step() returns early while a UI screen is open outside combat - that is S14 and it is correct; (2) loadState() DOES NOT CLOSE AN OPEN SCREEN - open the sheet, load arena_flat, mode is still 'sheet' and stepFrames(5) advances 0 frames; (3) so one screen left open by an earlier journey-run leg freezes every block of jrn06 and no loadState in it can recover. Signature: damagePlayer(1e5)+stepFrames produced NO death, NO surface, NO bloom - 20 rows of nulls, damage_frame 0 on all of them - and 10 of 19 checks carried pass:false while the console printed [OK] nineteen times. Directly reproduced in isolation.

M-D1's headline counts were CONSTANTS: trials_banked_eq_held/held_eq_stored were literally rows.length, so a run where all 20 rows failed the held==stored leg still printed 'trials_held_eq_stored: 20' next to 'mismatches_held_eq_stored: 20'. Now counts of rows that actually agreed.

M-D7 PASSES WITH A WORKING CONTROL (measured before the freeze was understood, and now re-gated): a real take+fenceSell moves six observables (fence purse, laundered rows, registry, save registry, inventory); across a death, zero of them move. The check now also asserts the death actually happened, because 'nothing moved' is only a fact about a death if there was one.

MY OWN GATE HAD THE BUG FIRST TIME: getFrame() returns a NUMBER (engine.sim.frame) while stepFrames() returns {frame,t_ms}; reading .frame off the former gave undefined and the gate refused to measure a healthy world with 'moved sim.frame by NaN'. Fixed to accept both shapes. Worth knowing for any probe that mixes the two.

THE GATE IS PROVED, 4/4, cheaply enough to take under loadavg 44. (1) CONTROL, healthy world: stepFrames(5) advances 5, surface up, deaths 0->1.
